short: The first naval battle in history fought entirely by aircraft, where opposing ships never sighted one another.
full:
Between 4 and 8 May 1942, naval forces of the United States and Australia engaged the Imperial Japanese Navy in the Coral Sea. The Japanese aimed to capture Port Moresby in New Guinea and Tulagi in the southeastern Solomon Islands to sever Allied supply lines. Thanks to signals intelligence, the Allies anticipated the move and deployed carrier task forces to intercept the invasion fleets.

It was a revolutionary engagement where opposing surface ships never fired upon or even sighted each other, relying solely on carrier-launched aircraft. Tactically, it was a Japanese victory as they sank the American carrier USS Lexington. Strategically, however, it was a pivotal Allied success: it marked the first time a Japanese advance was halted, and it deprived them of two fleet carriers that would otherwise have been available at the crucial Battle of Midway a month later.
